correctness.rationale: For all fixed \(0<p<1\) and positive speed/rate, the independent exponential isotropic steps have Gamma–Gaussian normal-mixture representation conditional on the geometric stopping index. At radii \(r_2>r_1>0\) the mixing-law Radon–Nikodym derivative \(\exp[-(r_2^2-r_1^2)/(2v)]\) is strictly increasing, hence every pairwise count-density likelihood ratio increases strictly; geometric priors preserve it. The marked Fourier transform splits exactly into a positive Bessel-K0 resolvent and an exponentially smaller positive subordination integral. Its complex-uniform expansion near marker \(z=1\) supplies the two exact cumulant slopes, shifts, derivative control, and moment-generating-function normal limit. All hypotheses and the \(r=0\) exclusion are explicit. The standalone verifier completed 275 numerical checks; these are corroborative and cannot replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The latent number of survived turning events is naturally inferred from a final observed terminal radius in the newly studied killed planar motion. Prior work supplies forward densities but not the inverse inferential shape. The strict MLR property yields global radial stochastic ordering and the Gaussian theorem yields quantitative large-radius uncertainty, with explicit linear and order-one terms. This is a structural inference result over all positive radii and all killing-index pairs, not an arbitrary special-value computation.
